passages.text: Control the “lake” of your own mind, else you cannot understand the lake of another ’s mind. The true teacher is one who can throw his whole force into the tendency of the taught. Without real sympathy we can never teach well.
passages.note: understanding and guiding others through sympathy

passages.text: Be honest and say, “I see the ideal but I cannot yet approach it”; but do not pretend to give up when you do not. If you give up, stand fast. If a hundred fall in the fight, seize the flag and carry it on. God is true for all that, no matter who fails. Let him who falls hand on the flag to another to carry on; it can never fall.
passages.note: honesty about falling short; carrying on after failure

passages.text: Give up and know that success will follow, even if you never see it. Jesus left twelve fishermen, and yet those few blew up the Roman Empire.
passages.note: work whose results you may never see

passages.text: He who struggles is better than he who never attempts.

Truth is to be judged by truth and by nothing else. Doing good is not the test of truth; the Sun needs no torch by which to see it. Even if truth destroys the whole universe, still it is truth; stand by it.
passages.note: standing by the truth regardless of cost

passages.text: The bullock in the oil-mill never reaches the wisp of hay tied in front of him, he only grinds out the oil. So we chase the will-o’-the-wisp of happiness that always eludes us, and we only grind nature’s mill, then die, merely to begin again. If we could get rid of evil, we should never catch a glimpse of anything higher; we would be satisfied and never struggle to get free. When man finds that all search for happiness in matter is nonsense, then religion begins.
passages.note: chasing happiness that always eludes us

passages.text: “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.” This sentence alone would save mankind if all books and prophets were lost.
passages.note: purity of heart as the essence

passages.text: The diabolical man is a part of my body as a wound or a burn is. We have to nurse it and get it better; so continually nurse and help the diabolical man, until he “heals” and is once happy and healthy.
passages.note: responding to cruel people with care

passages.text: Cry for help, and you will get it; and at last you will find that the one crying for help has vanished, and so has the Helper, and the play is over; only the Self remains.
